note: Multi-version cell: a clean single-season show (season 1, episode 1 — absoluteEpisode is just the plain episode index, 1) where the correct episode exists as THREE separate single-file candidates: 简 (zh-Hans, id 940940), 繁 (zh-Hant, id 940941), and 日 (Japanese, id 940942). Installing EITHER Chinese version is coverage-correct — no 简/繁 ranking — while installing the Japanese one is WRONG (not Chinese-language coverage). This is the "recognize Chinese, reject Japanese" test. All three candidates' download bodies are recorded (not just the expected one) so a real model may freely download/inspect any/all of them before deciding, exactly as it would need to when actually distinguishing script by content. KNOWN LIMITATION (not fixed here — out of scope for this phase, which only widened the language assertion): the runner's installedFilename/installedPath equality check is a single fixed string, but install_subtitle names the final file after the model's OWN chosen langTag, so a run that correctly installs the 繁 candidate instead of 简 would produce "Demon.Slayer.S01E01.zh-Hant.srt" and fail this cell's literal filename match despite being a coverage-correct outcome. candidateProviderId/installedFilename here are fixed to the 简 candidate as this fixture's documented expectation; a future runner enhancement could accept either filename for zh-any cells the same way it now accepts either installedLanguage.
